chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn Attiya from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a mature slave-girl, and she did not menstruate at his place until six months had passed for her, and there was no pregnancy in her. He said: 'If girls like her menstruate and it was not due to old age, then this is a defect, and she can be returned because of it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bought slave-girl does not menstruate within six months?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of '‘ayb' (defect) in the sale of slave-girls, specifically addressing the delay of menstruation as a potential flaw in the commodity. The ruling hinges on whether the delay is due to natural variation in age or an underlying condition, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on transparency and fairness in commercial transactions involving human beings.
